# Sāriputta Saṁyutta (SN 28)

**ID:** SN 28

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāriputtasaṁyutta* (SN 28) is the twenty-eighth collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated as the seventh chapter of the *Khandhavagga* [Bodhi 2003; Norman 1983]. The collection contains ten discourses centered on the Venerable Sāriputta [Norman 1983]. While Sāriputta is traditionally celebrated as the Buddha's foremost disciple in wisdom, this saṁyutta emphasizes his prowess as an adept in deep meditation [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003].

The first nine suttas (SN 28.1–9) share a repetitive, stereotyped structure [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003; Norman 1983]. In each, Ānanda notices Sāriputta's serene and radiant complexion and questions him about his state; Sāriputta explains how he progressively enters and emerges from each of the nine meditative attainments without any ego-affirming thoughts, identification, or sense of "I" [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003; Anālayo 2019]. In each case, Ānanda praises him, noting that Sāriputta has long eliminated all underlying tendencies to conceit and self-construing [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003; Anālayo 2019]. The tenth discourse (SN 28.10) departs from this pattern, presenting Sāriputta responding skillfully to the provocative questions of a female wanderer (Sucimukhī) and winning her approval [Tan 2002; Bodhi 2003].

 DharmaNexus also detects cross-language alignments with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) and *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), as well as Sanskrit treatises such as the *Mahāvyutpatti*, *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and *Dharmaskandha* [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records over 1,500 reuse matches with 95 texts, sharing extensive formulaic phrasing on meditative absorptions with the *Navakanipāta* (AN 9), *Moggallāna Saṁyutta* (SN 40), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), and *Kassapa Saṁyutta* (SN 16) [DharmaNexus].
